draft.title: Water and First Nations Australians
card: Rivers, waterholes, soaks and springs give people water to drink and food such as fish. They have done so for a very long time.
These places also carry cultural and spiritual meaning for First Nations Australians. Many are linked to stories and law handed down over generations.
Water places connect people to Country. Country means the land, waters and sky that a community belongs to and cares for.
Because of this, a waterhole is more than a water supply. It can be a place to be cared for, visited and respected.
draft.remember: For First Nations Australians, water places give water and food and also hold cultural and spiritual meaning tied to Country.

a.q: What does Country mean for First Nations Australians, in the case of water places?
opts: Land, waters and sky a community belongs to and cares for
A nation's border that is marked on a political map
A farming region that uses a river for irrigation
A park that is set aside to protect water for tourists
a.why: Country includes the land, waters and sky, and people have a living bond with it and care for it. The other options describe borders, farming or tourism, which are different ideas.
a.clue: Country is about belonging and caring, not borders.

b.q: A community visits a spring that gives fresh water and also holds sacred stories. Which statement best describes the spring's meaning?
opts: It gives water and also has cultural and spiritual meaning
It matters only as a source of drinking water
It matters only as a place with spiritual stories
It has meaning only when many tourists visit it
b.why: The card says these places give water and food and also carry cultural and spiritual meaning. The options with only are wrong because they leave out one of the two values.
b.clue: The spring matters in more than one way.

a.best: Land, waters and sky a community belongs to and cares for

b.best: It gives water and also has cultural and spiritual meaning

problems.detail: The stem already says the spring 'gives fresh water and also holds sacred stories', so the right option just restates it. All three wrong options use 'only', so a student can pick the right one without knowing the idea.

b.q: A community now gets piped water, so no one drinks from an old waterhole on its Country. Why might people still care for it?
opts: It carries cultural and spiritual meaning tied to Country
It remains the community's main drinking water supply
Its worth depends on how many tourists visit each year
Its value lasts only while people catch fish there
b.why: Water places are linked to stories and law and connect people to Country, so the waterhole can still matter when it is not used for water. The drinking water option is tempting, but the community now uses piped water, so that cannot be the reason.
b.clue: Think about what a water place means beyond water and food.
